beauty.summary: A booking-focused website for a lash, nail and hair studio, built as a template: every colour, size, text, photo and contact detail lives in one config, so the next client is a day of work instead of a rebuild.
points: Design tokens as the single source of truth: palette, type scale, spacing and motion timings in one file. Changing the primitives restyles the whole site.
Motion with intent: GSAP and Lenis, split-text reveals, a liquid chrome WebGL shape, depth sections such as tunnel, doors and card decks, a magnifier lens and a text scramble on hover.
Booking without a backend: a step-by-step wizard (service, first and backup day, time of day, name) that prepares a WhatsApp message. Nothing is stored or sent to a server.
Three languages and real SEO: DE, UK and EN with next-intl, sitemap, manifest, structured data, security headers and a strict content security policy.

noform.summary: A cinematic brand site for a fictional fashion label: one long scroll made of full-screen scenes, with sound, a strict mono type system and a restrained palette.
points: Scroll-driven scenes: GSAP ScrollTrigger and Observer run a sequence of full-screen scenes instead of a page of sections.
Motion studies: a lettering ring, a helix archive and a depth flight, each built as a separate experiment before it became part of the site.
A motion director that coordinates scene timing, the preloader and the sound toggle, with reduced-motion fallbacks.
Three languages (DE, EN, UK) with a typographic system that holds up in every one.

pizza.summary: A scroll storyboard for a pizza and döner delivery site: toppings lift and fall, the camera pivots, a yufka rolls in and the box opens, all on one scrubbed timeline.
points: Storyboard first: a written shot list with scroll percentages for every beat before any code.
2.5D sprite choreography: separate topping sprites on their own paths, with rotation, easing and landing spots.
Honest motion: where true 3D was not available, the sequence uses a cinematic cut instead of faking physics.
Mobile and reduced-motion variants: fewer sprites, shorter sequences and a static fallback.

ai.title: How I work with Claude Code: rules first
ai.summary: AI is fast. Rules make it reliable.
body: Every project has a CLAUDE.md: stack, design rules, a security checklist and things that never happen (no push without approval, no invented data, no secrets in the frontend).
Before large changes the codebase is mapped as a knowledge graph, so changes start from the architecture, not from guessing.
Work happens in small steps. Each step ends with build, lint and a real check in the browser.
Commits only happen when I say so. The AI proposes, I decide.
For languages I do not speak, the text is marked as AI-assisted and meant for a native speaker to review.

lh.title: Lighthouse from 74 to 94: what actually changed
lh.summary: Real measurements of this site, desktop, production build.
body: First measurement: Performance 74, Accessibility 97, Best practices 96, SEO 92, blocking time about 500 ms.
WebGL contexts and heavy canvases now start only when they are near the viewport. Blocking time dropped to about 0 ms and Performance reached 97.
A missing favicon returned a 404 and the canonical URL pointed to the wrong host. Both fixed: Best practices 100, SEO 100.
Small labels and decorative numbers had too little contrast, and the pull request demo used wrong ARIA roles and tiny buttons. Fixed: Accessibility 100.
After adding more features the score settled at Performance 94, Accessibility 100, Best practices 100, SEO 100. The numbers are stored with their date and re-measured after big changes.

decisions.title: Decisions behind this site
decisions.intro: Short decision records: the choice, the reason and the price I pay for it.

items.t: Next.js App Router with Server Components first
items.why: Fast first load and crawlable HTML for SEO, with client code only where interaction needs it.
items.price: More care with the boundary between server and client components.

items.t: CSS Modules and design tokens instead of Tailwind
items.why: Scoped styles, tokens as CSS variables, no extra dependency, and one place to restyle the whole site (see the design system page).
items.price: More CSS to write by hand. Tailwind is common in jobs, and I can pick it up with AI support.

items.t: GSAP and raw WebGL instead of a 3D library
items.why: The 3D effects here (water, orb, companion) are small shaders, so the bundle stays light and Lighthouse stays high.
items.price: More shader code to maintain by hand.

items.why: Four languages including right-to-left Arabic from one codebase, with hreflang and correct text direction.
items.price: Every layout must be checked in both directions.

items.t: Playwright end-to-end tests on the production build
items.why: The real risks of this site are layout overflow, languages, SEO tags and interaction, and only a real browser sees them.
items.price: Slower than unit tests. Unit tests with Vitest belong to business logic, as in ServiceOS.

items.t: Numbers stored with a date, not fetched live
items.why: Lighthouse scores, test results and the contribution graph are saved at build time. No third-party request from your browser, and no number without a date.
items.price: They can be out of date until I measure again.

items.why: Simple and GDPR-friendly for a personal site.
items.price: No usage data until the site is online and Search Console is connected.

a11y.title: Accessibility statement
a11y.intro: I aim for WCAG 2.2 level AA. This is a self-assessment, not a formal audit.
done: Semantic HTML, one H1 per page and a logical heading order.
Keyboard access with a visible focus on every interactive element.
Text contrast of at least 4.5 to 1, checked in light and dark theme (see the design system page).
Animation switches off with the system setting prefers-reduced-motion.
Touch targets of at least 24 pixels.
Right-to-left layout for Arabic with logical CSS properties.
Automated checks: Lighthouse accessibility 100 and Playwright tests on every pull request.
limits: The 3D and WebGL effects are decorative and hidden from assistive technology, but pinned scroll scenes can be demanding for some people.
The Arabic text is written with AI tools and has not been reviewed by a native speaker.
The PDF profile cards are generated from HTML and may not be fully accessible. The plain-text CV page is the accessible version.
I have not run a test with screen reader users yet.
a11y.contact: If something does not work for you, please write to me. I will answer and fix what I can.
